_readme: A REGISTER, NOT A CENSUS. Every other number in this project is something the collector saw
for itself and can show you a raw capture for. Nothing in this file is. These are facts read
out of company filings, exchange announcements and the trade press, typed in by hand, each
carrying the date it was true, how sure we are, and where it came from.
Consequently: a missing count is written as null and never guessed, and 'no_evidence' means
we did not find a presence, NOT that there is none. Those are different claims and the
register refuses to blur them.
WHAT GETS A ROW. Two tests, and only two: the chain originates in China, and there is
evidence it trades in a market this project covers. Whether we can COLLECT it is not a test.
A register that admitted only the chains with a convenient locator would describe the subset
that is easy to scrape and call it the world — and it would quietly drop Pop Mart, Cotti and
Yang's Braised Chicken, which are among the most interesting entries in it. Collectability
decides the METHOD (a daily adapter, or a hand-typed row with its reason recorded), never the
membership. Size in China is not a test either: a chain with 20,000 domestic stores and no
foreign shopfront belongs to a different subject.
ORIGIN AND DESTINATION ARE DIFFERENT AXES, which is what lets Hong Kong sit in this list.
The project collects chains that ORIGINATE in China; Taiwanese and Hong Kong brands
are out of scope as origins. Hong Kong as a DESTINATION is another matter: it is part of
China politically and a separate retail market practically — its own currency, rents, labour
market, tastes and regulator. A Zhengzhou chain opening in Mong Kok is making the same kind
of bet it makes in Singapore, at smaller scale. The register says so and lets the reader
disagree, rather than deciding the question by leaving the row out.
Reviewed periodically rather than daily — `python -m chain_atlas register --stale` lists
what has not been looked at in 90 days.

HK.name: Hong Kong
HK.note: Part of China politically, a separate retail market practically. Included as a destination, never as an origin — see the readme.

chicjoc.name: CHICJOC
chicjoc.global: Shanghai "minimalist-luxury" (极简极奢) womenswear brand (operator Shanghai Jiuci Brand Management, 上海玖赐; founded 2015). Began online on Taobao, went offline in May 2022 (first store Nanjing Deji Plaza) and grew to ~40–50 brick-and-mortar stores across first- and key second-tier Chinese cities' high-end malls, with four own factories. Overseas since Nov 2024 — US (Los Angeles + Newport Beach, CA) and France (Paris). No Chinese brand name (uses CHICJOC).
chicjoc.franchise_note: Shanghai womenswear chain; US-tracked via its two California stores, with a Paris store abroad. No US franchise offer or FDD confirmed.

babakehouse.name: BA Artisan Bakehouse
babakehouse.global: French-Asian artisan bakery chain (BA / BON APPÉTIT), founded 2016 in Kunming, Yunnan; operator Yunnan Bangnaboudi Food Development Co. (邦纳博地). ~45 stores across China (Kunming, Chongqing, Xi'an, Chengdu…) plus overseas in Dubai and the US; its North America flagship is in Bellevue, WA. No formal Chinese brand name — written BA / BA烘焙.
babakehouse.franchise_note: Yunnan bakery chain; US-tracked via its Bellevue, WA flagship, with a Dubai store abroad. No US franchise offer or FDD confirmed.

caoshiyabo.name: Caoshiyabo
caoshiyabo.global: China-origin braised duck-neck (卤味) snack brand traced to a ~2003 street cart (Changsha, Hunan / Chengdu); ~2,000+ franchised stores across 300+ Chinese cities. The name is CONTESTED — multiple separate China companies (成都团结曹氏, 成都蜀湘曹氏, 湖南曹氏鸭脖) operate under it amid trademark disputes, so no single corporate owner is asserted here. Present in Malaysia (Kuala Lumpur, Selangor, Johor); the local 'Caoshiyabo Malaysia' operation's exact China parent / authorization is unconfirmed. No US presence.
caoshiyabo.franchise_note: Contested, fragmented China 卤味 brand (multiple entities, trademark disputes); Malaysia stores brand as 'Caoshiyabo Malaysia' with parent unconfirmed. No US locations.

ningji.name: Ningji Lemon Tea
ningji.global: 3,000+ hand-smashed-lemon-tea (手打柠檬茶) stores; founded 2021 in Changsha, Hunan (founder Wang Jie; Tencent/ByteDance/Shunwei-backed). Overseas since 2025 — open in Malaysia, Singapore and Cambodia, with Australia and New Zealand signed. Its US entry, branded 'Bobobaba' (Glendale, CA), opened in April 2026 and closed within months.
ningji.franchise_note: China 手打柠檬茶 franchise; its sole US store traded as 'Bobobaba' (now closed). No US franchise offer or FDD. A different company from NingQi 柠気 (Yunnan).

ningqi.name: NingQi
ningqi.global: Yunnan glutinous-rice-scented tea brand (糯米香叶 / 东方香茶); founded October 2021 in Yunnan (founder Huang Lei). 200+ stores across 30+ Chinese cities within a year; overseas debut in Malaysia (Sutera Mall, Johor Bahru). No US presence.
ningqi.franchise_note: Yunnan 糯米香 tea chain; no US locations. A different company from Ningji 柠季 (Changsha, Hunan) despite the near-identical name.

bingxue.name: BINGXUE
bingxue.global: Shandong tea-and-ice-cream chain (冰雪时光, Tai'an 2014); the bear-mascot budget rival to Mixue, with about 5,000 stores across 18 countries, 1,500+ outside its home market. Entered the US (Davis, CA) on 2 Oct 2026.
bingxue.franchise_note: Franchise-driven at home and abroad; US entry is new (first store Davis, CA, Oct 2026) — no US franchise offer or FDD confirmed yet.

mixue.name: MIXUE
mixue.global: 59,823 stores worldwide at 31 Dec 2025; about 4,700 of them outside China across 13 countries
mixue.franchise_note: Open US franchise — join.mixueusfranchise.com (Snow King (US) Corp); ~$10K fee, 2% royalty, ~$272K-843K total per its own US FDD (first-party, not state-verified); applications open in NY/CA/MA.

chagee.name: CHAGEE
chagee.franchise_note: US deliberately company-owned (~9 CA stores); heavily franchised in China/Asia but no US franchise offer.

luckin.name: Luckin Coffee
luckin.global: surpassed 38,000 stores globally by Sept 2026 (China, Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, US)
luckin.franchise_note: US stores company-operated; no US franchise offer or FDD (China mixes self-operated + partnership).

cotti.name: Cotti Coffee
cotti.global: 18,000+ stores in 28 countries as of April 2026
cotti.franchise_note: New US franchise via Cotti Partners LLC (Delaware); 2026 US FDD; ~$259K-608K total. Legacy US stores were a license network; franchise is the go-forward path.

miniso.name: MINISO
miniso.global: 8,485 stores at 31 Dec 2025, of which 3,583 overseas
miniso.franchise_note: Franchising in the US since 2018 via Miniso Depot Franchisor LLC; registered US FDDs (2021/2023/2025); 'MINISO Partner' consignment/purchase tracks, ~$20-30K fee. Best-documented open US offer.

popmart.name: POP MART
popmart.global: 630 retail stores and 2,637 roboshops at end-2025, across more than 30 countries and regions; overseas sales are over 40% of revenue.
popmart.franchise_note: Does not franchise anywhere; US is wholly company-owned stores + robo-shops + wholesale.

heytea.name: HEYTEA
heytea.global: 4,000+ stores; over 100 of them overseas across 8 countries and 28 cities
heytea.franchise_note: First-party US 'partnership' franchise (aboutPartnersEn): $300K+ liquidity, ~$50K fee/3yr, 3% royalty, ~$295K-507K total; applications reopened Sept 2025. No confirmed US-registered FDD.

haidilao.name: Haidilao
haidilao.global: Overseas arm Super Hi International (HKEX 9658 / Nasdaq HDL) runs ~120-125 restaurants in markets such as Singapore, Japan, Korea, the US, the UK, Canada and Australia; the Haidilao parent separately runs Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan — which is why those were absent from Super Hi's overseas store list.
haidilao.franchise_note: US/NA stores company-owned (Super Hi Int'l); franchising is China-only. No US franchise offer.

yangs.name: Yang's Braised Chicken Rice
yangs.global: 6,000+ locations, overwhelmingly in China; abroad since 2017
yangs.franchise_note: Yang's Braised Chicken Rice USA — franchising in the US since ~2018; registered US FDD; ~$35K fee, 6% royalty + 2% marketing, ~$258K-538K total. Actively franchising in CA.

taier.name: Tai Er
taier.global: 482 Tai Er outlets at March 2026; parent Jiumaojiu (HKEX 9922) ran 31 restaurants outside China at H1 2025, up from 22
taier.franchise_note: US stores run directly by parent Jiumaojiu; Tai Er franchising is China-only.

juewei.name: Juewei
juewei.global: 16,000+ outlets; trades as King of Braise in Singapore — the same naming trap as ChaPanda/TeaByDo
juewei.franchise_note: Heavily franchised in China (10,000+); only North-American arm is Canada (BC). No US-specific open application or US FDD found; US presence appears informal.

nayuki.name: Naixue
nayuki.global: HKEX 2150; rebranded from Nayuki to Naixue. Trades overseas — US, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Japan — as Naisnow (Tea & Bakery).
nayuki.franchise_note: US entry direct/company-operated; China 'Partner Plan' franchising (from Jul 2023) is China-only.

chabaidao.name: ChaPanda
chabaidao.global: HKEX 2555; 8,700+ stores worldwide. Trades as ChaPanda in English and as TeaByDo in North America
chabaidao.franchise_note: First US store Aug 2025 (Flushing) as a direct rollout; heavily franchised in China; intl master/area via VF (Asia/MENA), not US. No first-party US franchise application or US FDD found.

yangguofu.name: Yangguofu
yangguofu.global: 6,000+ malatang outlets, overwhelmingly in China, as of 2025; US franchising began 2024
yangguofu.franchise_note: Open first-party US franchise application (ygfus.com/franchise.html; asks net assets >$500K); backed by a registered US FDD (Captain Business Management Co., Minnesota franchise registration #11645 — the source of our US store roster). Fee/royalty not disclosed on the site.

fishwithyou.name: Fish With You
fishwithyou.global: sauerkraut-fish (酸菜鱼) fast-casual chain, several thousand outlets in China (2025 est.); US franchising began 2024-25
fishwithyou.franchise_note: Sauerkraut-fish franchise (2,700+); many US locations and a public 'US 1,000 cities' recruiting push suggest US units are franchised, but no confirmed first-party US application page or US FDD found.

zhangliang.name: Zhang Liang Malatang
zhangliang.global: one of China's two dominant malatang chains, ~6,000 outlets, founded in Harbin in 2008; its own brand news reports 42 North American outlets across the US, Canada and Mexico as of Sept 2026
zhangliang.franchise_note: Open US franchise application on first-party US site (zlmalatang.us/franchise); many US stores. Fee/royalty/FDD not publicly disclosed.

chahalo.name: ChaHalo
chahalo.global: premium modern-Chinese-tea chain founded in Xi'an in 2016, ~1,000 stores across China; began overseas expansion in 2024, now in the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and the UK
chahalo.franchise_note: Entered the US in 2025 as company-driven expansion (NY/CA/TX/MD); its 'Join ChaHalo' page is China-market. No open US franchise offer found.

xiaolongkan.name: Shoo Loong Kan Hotpot
xiaolongkan.global: Sichuan hotpot chain from Chengdu (2014), thousands of outlets in China; trades in the US as Shoo Loong Kan Hotpot and publishes its own US locator (8 open + 4 coming soon, Sept 2026)
xiaolongkan.franchise_note: First-party US franchise page (shooloongkan.us/franchise) with a 4-step application; ~7 US stores. Fee/royalty/FDD not disclosed.

yihetang.name: Yihetang
yihetang.global: 8,000+ contracted stores (Dec 2024), overwhelmingly China; ~60 international stores in a Vietnam-Thailand-Malaysia-Indonesia SE-Asia cluster (early 2026)
yihetang.franchise_note: 8,000+ franchises but China + SE Asia only; no US presence or offer.

tianlala.name: Tianlala
tianlala.global: ~8,000 China stores + 200+ overseas (Feb 2025); trademarks in 52 countries; overseas ops HQ Singapore (2023), SE Asia + Central Asia focus
tianlala.franchise_note: 8,000+ China franchises, ~200 international (Philippines etc.); no US presence or offer.

luckycup.name: Lucky Cup
luckycup.global: Mixue's budget coffee arm; hit 10,000 stores (Nov 2025), almost all in China; overseas brand-new
luckycup.franchise_note: Mixue's low-cost coffee sub-brand (NOT Luckin); 10,000+ China franchises + SE Asia; no US.

yujianxiaomian.name: Yu Jian Xiao Mian
yujianxiaomian.global: ~500+ stores worldwide (Chongqing noodles, HKEX-listed Dec 2025); overseas since Dec 2025 and scaling in Hong Kong (19 stores by Oct 2026) plus 4 in Singapore
yujianxiaomian.franchise_note: China/HK chain; no US locations (the DC 'Yu Noodles' is an unrelated US brand).

happylamb.name: Happy Lamb Hot Pot
happylamb.global: ~100+ Inner-Mongolian-style hot pot restaurants across ~11 countries. Re-founded 2017 by Zhang Gang (张钢), the founder of Little Sheep (小肥羊), after Yum! Brands acquired Little Sheep; first store Baotou (Inner Mongolia) Dec 2017, then Hohhot and Shijiazhuang. North American operations are run from a Houston, TX base.
happylamb.franchise_note: Inner Mongolian hot pot from the Little Sheep founder. The US estate (29 outlets across 11 states) is collected on the map and run from Houston; no registered US franchise offering found in state registries.

bingz.name: Bingz
bingz.global: Shaanxi roujiamo (肉夹馍) fast-food chain — the 'crispy 'wich' — founded Beijing 2014; stores across Beijing, Tianjin, Xi'an, Zhengzhou and more. Launched its international 'Bingz' brand in 2018; entered Canada 2021 (first Chinese fast-food brand to operate directly in North America, ~7 GTA stores) and Singapore, and opened its first US store (San Gabriel CA) on 2 Oct 2026. WATCH: aggressive US expansion planned — a $50M US raise and a stated 300-US-store goal — so new US outlets are expected.
bingz.franchise_note: Beijing roujiamo fast-food chain. US entry Oct 2026 (San Gabriel); the US estate is tracked on the map via sightings (chain_id 'bingz'). US-EXPANSION WATCH: with a $50M US raise and a 300-US-store plan announced, this is a chain to watch for rapid US growth — the daily lead-discovery routine checks for new Bingz US outlets (as a tracked chain) and launch-watch monitors bingz.com for a US store locator / rising store count.

teapulse.name: Teapulse
teapulse.global: 悸动烧仙草 (Jidong), a Shanghai new-tea / grass-jelly (烧仙草) chain ~19 years old with 2,000+ locations; began expanding abroad in 2019 (UK, Japan, Philippines, Laos, South Korea). Trades in the US as 'Teapulse' (first store Flushing NY ~2022, then a Manhattan expansion through 2026) and abroad as 'Jidong' / 'Jidong Herbal Jelly'.
teapulse.franchise_note: Shanghai grass-jelly / new-tea chain. US estate (~7 NYC outlets) trades as Teapulse and is tracked on the map via sightings (chain_id 'teapulse'); teapulseusa.com/locations is a dynamic Wix widget with no readable store feed.

hefu.name: Hefu Noodle
hefu.global: 632 stores (2025) across 80+ Chinese cities; overseas began in Hong Kong Feb 2024
hefu.franchise_note: Began franchising Apr 2024 — China only (~600 stores); no US stores or offer.

xiabu.name: Xiabu Xiabu
xiabu.global: ~1,000+ outlets across the Xiabu + Coucou brands, overwhelmingly in China; the Xiabu brand's footprint outside China is ~21 across HK/Taiwan/Macau/Singapore (Jun 2024)
xiabu.franchise_note: No US restaurants (only packaged hotpot products via Weee); China/HK company-operated.

coucou.name: Coucou
coucou.global: Xiabu Xiabu's premium sub-brand (2016); ~200 branches mostly in China + Hong Kong; outside China in Hong Kong and Singapore
coucou.franchise_note: Xiabu Xiabu's premium hotpot+tea brand; China/HK/Singapore only; no US.

laowang.name: Laowang
laowang.global: China's largest pork-tripe-chicken (猪肚鸡) hotpot chain, ~135-150 restaurants in China; its only confirmed store outside China is one in Taipei
laowang.franchise_note: Directly operated; China (and Spain); no confirmed US location or franchise offer.

peijie.name: Peijie
peijie.global: Chongqing hotpot, ~30 mostly directly-operated stores in China; first overseas store Amsterdam (Oct 2025)
peijie.franchise_note: Chongqing hotpot; expanded to Amsterdam, not the US.

zhouheiya.name: Zhou Hei Ya
zhouheiya.global: ~1,000+ braised-duck snack stores, almost all in China (HK-listed 1458.HK — a stock listing only); a single overseas store
zhouheiya.franchise_note: Began China franchising 2019-20; no US stores (products sold online only).

kkv.name: KKV
kkv.global: KK Group's lead overseas retail brand; the group has >1,000 China stores + 170+ overseas across 6 SE-Asian countries (Jun 2026)
kkv.franchise_note: KK Group variety-store brand; expanding in SE Asia, not the US.

x11.name: X11
x11.global: KK Group art-toy/trend retail brand (~64 stores Jan 2024, mostly China); a later overseas entrant, part of the group's 170+ overseas
x11.franchise_note: KK Group trend-toy brand (NOT Pop Mart); SE Asia expansion; no US presence.

colorist.name: The Colorist
colorist.global: KK Group cosmetics retail brand (2019); part of the group's 170+ overseas stores
colorist.franchise_note: KK Group beauty-retail; China company-owned + franchise mix; no US stores or offer.

cooltoy.name: Cool Toy
cooltoy.global: Ningbo art-toy retailer (~300 stores in 60+ Chinese cities); overseas nascent, retrenching domestically
cooltoy.franchise_note: Opened China franchising in 2022 (~300 stores), China-only; no US presence.

muwu.name: Muwu BBQ
muwu.global: ~400+ directly-operated skewer/BBQ stores across ~20 Chinese cities; overseas early-stage (Hong Kong)
muwu.franchise_note: 400+ direct-operated stores, explicitly not franchised; no US franchise.

steelpipe.name: Steel Pipe No.5
steelpipe.name_zh: 钢管厂五区小郡肝串串香
steelpipe.global: ~880 skewer-hotpot (串串香) stores (Nov 2025), overwhelmingly in China; overseas is franchise-driven and name-fragmented, so attributions are brand-name-level, not corporate-confirmed
steelpipe.franchise_note: Franchises globally (853 stores incl. some US/Canada/Australia); no US FDD or first-party US franchise page found; likely area/master deals abroad.

micun.name: Micun
micun.global: 1,900+ Korean-style bibimbap fast-food stores, nearly all in China; overseas footprint = Singapore only
micun.franchise_note: Officially directly-operated only; states it does not franchise (warns offers are scams).

greentea.name: Green Tea
greentea.global: China-origin 'New Zhejiang Cuisine' (新浙江菜) casual-dining chain — founded in Hangzhou, Zhejiang by chairman Wang Qinsong 王勤松 (group marked its 20th anniversary in 2024); ~500-700 stores, overwhelmingly in China; HKEX-listed 2025 (6831). Overseas expansion began 31 Aug 2024 with Hong Kong (Hysan Place), then The Wai Mall (Nov 2024) and SE Asia. Signature Zhejiang dishes (West Lake water-shield & fish-ball soup, Dongpo braised beef); bamboo-themed 'Jiangnan' interiors.
greentea.franchise_note: 470+ directly-operated; officially no franchising (warns offers are fraudulent); US only in planning.

tanyu.name: Tanyu
tanyu.global: China-origin grilled-fish (烤魚) chain — founded Shenzhen 2013 (parent Gantang Mingshan 甘棠明善, Shenzhen); signature fresh-green-pepper grilled fish. 400+ stores across 80+ China cities; overseas across ~8 markets incl. Singapore (first flagship 2017), Malaysia (KL 2023) and Hong Kong. An earlier note cited North American outlets (a Flushing NY store and Vancouver), but a Tanyu is NOT currently observed in Flushing (Oct 2026) — US/Canada presence unconfirmed.
tanyu.franchise_note: Franchises in China. An earlier note reported a Flushing NY store + Vancouver, but no Tanyu is currently observed in Flushing — US/NA presence unconfirmed, no US FDD or first-party US franchise page. HK 2 outlets.

nanjingimpressions.name: Nanjing Impressions
nanjingimpressions.global: ~35-40 Nanjing-cuisine stores, all in China except a single overseas outlet
nanjingimpressions.franchise_note: ~40 outlets (China + Singapore), directly operated; no US presence or offer.

nowwa.name: Nowwa Coffee
nowwa.global: ~10,000 stores (Dec 2025) across 300+ cities, grown largely through Meiyijia convenience-store counters; overseas since 2024 — Macau, then its first standalone overseas store in Melbourne (Apr 2025) and Indonesia (Jan 2026), with more of Southeast Asia signed. North America is a stated expansion target in the company's own materials (and secondary coverage), but with no US city, franchise partner or date yet — watchlist, not announced.
nowwa.franchise_note: Shop-in-shop/partner franchise, 10,000+ China outlets; no US stores or offer.

manner.name: Manner Coffee
manner.global: Premium 'street coffee' chain founded 2015 in Shanghai, ~1,000 stores in China; making its first move outside China with a Hong Kong store (announced 2026, signage 'Maners Coffee').
manner.franchise_note: 100% company-operated; publicly states it does not franchise anywhere; China-only.

yuanji.name: Yuanji Chuanchuanxiang
yuanji.global: Chengdu skewer-hotpot chain (founded 1996; distinct from the 袁记云饺 dumpling brand); claims industry-first overseas direct stores from 2016 in Canada, then the Netherlands and Australia.
yuanji.franchise_note: Franchises heavily in China (4,773 global) + some overseas direct stores; no US offer or FDD.

xiaogujiejie.name: Xiaogujiejie
xiaogujiejie.global: Tianjin malatang chain (founded 2018), 1,000+ stores by Aug 2026. Company and trade press describe overseas stores across Japan, France, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, Australia, Singapore and the US, but few are independently confirmed.
xiaogujiejie.franchise_note: Malatang franchise (China terms ~RMB19,800 fee); claims a US store but no US FDD or first-party US franchise page found.

banu.name: Banu Maodu Hotpot
banu.global: Premium Henan hotpot chain (founded 2001, Anyang; ~240 directly-operated stores per banu.cn, Oct 2026). Going global with its first overseas store — Hysan Place, Causeway Bay, Hong Kong, opening mid-November 2026, with a stated plan for 15–20 Hong Kong stores.
banu.franchise_note: ~240 stores, all self-operated (banu.cn Oct 2026; 162 at the 2025 HK IPO); founder eyeing North America but no US store or franchise yet.

laoxiangji.name: Laoxiangji
laoxiangji.global: Hefei home-style chicken chain; opened its first overseas store in 2026 (Malaysia). Trades overseas as Lausanjee (Malaysia open; Singapore JV with Jumbo Group, 2026).
laoxiangji.franchise_note: China direct + franchise mix since 2020 (~1,900 stores); China-only, no US franchise.

manling.name: Manling Congee
manling.global: Shanghai congee chain; overseas debut 2025 in Malaysia, then Spain.
manling.franchise_note: Delivery-focused franchise chain; heavy China franchising; no US presence or offer.

xiaocaiyuan.name: Xiao Cai Yuan
xiaocaiyuan.global: Anhui home-style (徽菜) chain, HK-listed (HKEX 0999); announced Hong Kong as its overseas debut.
xiaocaiyuan.franchise_note: Self-operated homestyle dining in China (~300+); does not franchise; no US presence.

linlee.name: LINLEE
linlee.global: Foshan (Guangdong) tea brand; overseas expansion began with Hong Kong.
linlee.franchise_note: Franchises in China only (~2,000); international expansion 'planned 2026'; no US store or franchise offer.

moreyogurt.name: More Yogurt
moreyogurt.global: Shanghai yogurt-drink chain (its own English name is 'More Yogurt'); operates in Hong Kong, Malaysia and Singapore, and opened its first US store in Tustin, California in 2026.
moreyogurt.franchise_note: Franchises in China; US entry (Tustin, CA) is brand-led; no US FDD or open US franchise application.

moge.name: Möge Tee
moge.global: Chinese bubble-tea chain (愿茶, trades in the US as 'Möge Tee'); founded 2012, franchised from 2018. Its US estate is collected daily from its own locator (mogeteeusa.com): ~70 stores across 18 states as of Oct 2026. A different brand from Molly Tea (茉莉奶白).
moge.franchise_note: Moge Tee USA Franchising LLC — US FDD (2022/2023); $40K fee, 3% royalty + 2% marketing, ~$159K-269K total; open first-party US application; 75+ US units.

mstand.name: M Stand
mstand.global: Shanghai specialty-coffee chain (founded 2017); first overseas store in Japan.
mstand.franchise_note: Direct + some franchise in China (~500 stores); no US stores or franchise offer.

meiyijia.name: Meiyijia
meiyijia.global: Dongguan convenience-store chain; expanding into Southeast Asia, partly under an 'Ohmee' brand.
meiyijia.franchise_note: China's largest convenience franchise (~38,000) but China-only; overseas push is SE Asia.

crvanguard.name: CR Vanguard
crvanguard.global: China Resources supermarket group; long-established in Hong Kong.
crvanguard.franchise_note: State-owned supermarket (China Resources); operates in China and Hong Kong only.

qiandama.name: Qiandama
qiandama.global: Dongguan fresh-food/grocery chain; 72 stores across Hong Kong and Macau (2025), branded QDAMA.
qiandama.franchise_note: Fresh-grocery franchise in China (Pearl River Delta) only; no US presence.

bestore.name: Bestore
bestore.global: Wuhan packaged-snack retailer; first branded overseas flagship in Malaysia.
bestore.franchise_note: US reach is distribution/retailers (H-Mart, Weee, Amazon) + a Times Square pop-up; not a franchise.

mglife.name: M&G LIFE
mglife.global: M&G/Chenguang lifestyle-stationery retailer (Jiumu Sundry Social); expanding in Southeast Asia.
mglife.franchise_note: Company-run lifestyle retail in China/Asia; US only via Amazon wholesale; no US stores or franchise.

anta.name: Anta
anta.global: China's largest sportswear group (~9,900 Anta-brand stores); Southeast Asia expansion (targeting ~1,000 stores by 2028) with a first US flagship in Beverly Hills (Feb 2026).
anta.franchise_note: First US store (Beverly Hills, 2026) directly operated — DTC pivot; no US franchise.

urbanrevivo.name: Urban Revivo
urbanrevivo.global: Guangzhou fast-fashion chain (400+ large-format stores, parent FMG); overseas in SE Asia, Hong Kong, the UK and (Feb 2025) the US (SoHo).
urbanrevivo.franchise_note: US debut is a company-operated SoHo NYC flagship; no US FDD or open franchise application.

jnby.name: JNBY
jnby.global: Hangzhou designer-apparel house (~2,118 stores across JNBY and its sister brands); overseas in Canada and the US, where it trades as AGoodFun via a local licensee.
jnby.franchise_note: US stores run by JNBY USA / authorized partner; apparel brand, no US franchise or FDD.

meilleurmoment.name: Meilleur Moment
meilleurmoment.global: Womenswear line of Hangzhou's Eifini group (600+ stores group-wide); overseas boutiques in France, Singapore and (May 2025) the US (SoHo).
meilleurmoment.franchise_note: Eifini Group brand; US entry is a company-operated SoHo NYC flagship. No franchise offer.

bosideng.name: Bosideng
bosideng.global: Changshu down-jacket maker; a London flagship (reopened Oct 2022). European sales are otherwise wholesale.
bosideng.franchise_note: US reach is marketplaces + own DTC e-commerce; no US retail franchise.

semir.name: Semir
semir.global: Wenzhou mass-apparel group (森马服饰): Semir adult casual + Balabala 巴拉巴拉 kidswear (China's largest kidswear brand). 100+ overseas stores across ~15 markets — overseas/HK retail runs overwhelmingly under the Balabala banner.
semir.franchise_note: China ~42% franchised but global franchise reps cover SE Asia/Russia/Middle East, not the US; US entered via e-commerce only.

xtep.name: Xtep
xtep.global: Quanzhou sportswear/running brand; mono-brand 'retail+community' stores in Malaysia and Singapore.
xtep.franchise_note: Distributor + franchise network globally (~8,100 stores); no US stores or US franchise program; US reach online/marketplace.

laopu.name: Laopu Gold
laopu.global: Beijing heritage-gold jeweller; Hong Kong and Macau, plus a first true overseas store in Singapore (Jun 2025).
laopu.franchise_note: ~41 directly operated boutiques, no franchising; no US presence.

lining.name: Li-Ning
lining.global: Beijing sportswear brand; a Hong Kong flagship (2022) and Southeast-Asia plans. An earlier US store (Portland) has closed.
lining.franchise_note: US served by a distributor (LN Distribution); China company+franchise hybrid; no US FDD or open US franchise.

moco.name: MO&Co.
moco.global: Guangzhou contemporary womenswear; standalone stores in Paris, London and Malaysia.
moco.franchise_note: EPO Fashion Group brand; US orders/shipping suspended; no US franchise or license program.

icicle.name: Icicle
icicle.global: Shanghai premium apparel house (owns France's Carven); boutiques in Paris incl. a 35 Av. George V flagship.
icicle.franchise_note: ~106 directly operated boutiques + department-store wholesale; US via multi-brand retailers; no franchise.

cabbeen.name: Cabbeen
cabbeen.global: Foshan designer menswear; first overseas stores in Malaysia, with more planned.
cabbeen.franchise_note: China revenue via company-operated + franchise + wholesale; no US stores or US franchise program.

florasis.name: Florasis
florasis.global: Hangzhou heritage-cosmetics brand; a Tokyo flagship (Jan 2025) and a Paris counter (2024). US reach is retail shelves only.
florasis.franchise_note: US is DTC only (own site + Amazon + TikTok Shop); no physical stores, no franchise.

maogeping.name: Mao Geping
maogeping.global: Prestige-makeup house (first HK-listed C-beauty, 1318); a department-counter model with a first overseas store in Hong Kong (2025).
maogeping.franchise_note: Self-operated counters in Chinese department stores + e-commerce; US only via third-party resellers; no franchise.

judydoll.name: Judydoll
judydoll.global: Shanghai color cosmetics brand (Joy Group); standalone stores in Singapore and Hong Kong.
judydoll.franchise_note: US via Amazon flagship + cross-border e-commerce (Joy Group); no franchise.

joocyee.name: Joocyee
joocyee.global: Shanghai color cosmetics brand (Joy Group, sister to Judydoll); first international store in Singapore.
joocyee.franchise_note: US via own site, TikTok Shop and cross-border retailers (Joy Group); no franchise.

xiaomi.name: Xiaomi
xiaomi.global: Consumer-electronics giant; 100+ own/franchised Mi Stores across Europe (incl. Poland), plus India, SE Asia and the Middle East. No US retail.
xiaomi.franchise_note: No US Mi Stores; US via Best Buy co-listing + third-party importers; Mi Store franchise/distributor programs exist only outside the US.

huawei.name: Huawei
huawei.global: Consumer-electronics maker; branded 'experience stores' across Europe (Madrid, Milan, Barcelona, Paris, Vienna). No US presence.
huawei.franchise_note: FCC bars authorization/sale of new Huawei devices; no authorized US retailers; US only via gray-market importers. No US franchise.

hotmaxx.name: HotMaxx
hotmaxx.global: Shanghai soft-discount / near-expiry snack & packaged-goods retailer (~950 stores); a Hong Kong store (Sep 2024), Japan announced.
hotmaxx.franchise_note: Opened China franchising Apr 2023 (~950 stores); international began Osaka 2025; no US entry or franchise.

malubianbian.name: Malubianbian
malubianbian.global: Chengdu skewer-style (chuàn-chuàn) hot pot chain founded 2015 (2016 per some sources); more than 1,000 outlets in and outside China by 2021. In the US since 2019 (Los Angeles / Rowland Heights), trading as MLBB / Ma Lu Bian Bian.
malubianbian.franchise_note: Heavily franchised (1,000+); ~5 US restaurants (Houston, Tustin, Orlando, Philadelphia) but no US FDD or open first-party US franchise application found; US units likely area-developer/licensed, unconfirmed.

makkee.name: Makkee Dessert
makkee.global: 麦记牛奶 (Mak Kee Milk Company), a Chinese dessert-soup (糖水/炖奶) chain founded 2021 in Huzhou, Zhejiang (founder Xu Kang) — milk-based takes on traditional Chinese tong sui. China's largest Chinese-dessert-soup chain by store count, ~1,000 outlets (up from ~53 at the start of 2025). Began expanding abroad in 2025: the United States (CA/NY/WA, trading as 'Makkee Dessert') and Australia (Sydney). Despite the Cantonese-style 'Mak Kee' branding it is Zhejiang-born, not Hong Kong.
makkee.franchise_note: Chinese dessert-soup chain. US estate (~6 outlets: Rowland Heights / San Gabriel / Mountain View / DTLA CA, Flushing NY, Bellevue WA; Irvine CA, San Jose CA, Brooklyn NY announced) trades as Makkee Dessert and is tracked on the map via sightings (chain_id 'makkee') — no readable US locator (Chowbus orders). No US FDD found and US franchising not advertised (0 = none found).

guoquan.name: Guoquan
guoquan.global: Chinese home-dining-ingredients retailer (锅圈食汇 / GQ Homepot; HKEX 2517, listed Nov 2023) — hot pot and BBQ ingredient packs, ready-to-cook and ready-to-eat meals; more than 11,500 stores in China at the end of 2025. Opened its first store outside its home market on 19 Aug 2026, a Wan Chai flagship in Hong Kong with in-store dining, and set up its international regional HQ there as the launchpad for Southeast Asia, Europe and North America.
guoquan.franchise_note: Chinese hot-pot/BBQ home-ingredient retail chain (HKEX 2517). International expansion began Aug 2026 from a Hong Kong flagship + regional HQ; no US presence yet.

commune.name: COMMUNE
commune.global: Chinese restaurant-bar ('dining bar') chain (COMMUNE / 幻师), founded 2016 in Wuhan, HQ Zhuhai, Guangdong (Jiwu Siwei / Zhuhai Tangqi Shengtao) — a 'super bar + self-serve drinks + dining' format; ~112 directly-operated stores across 40 Chinese cities (Sep 2025). Opened its first store outside its home market on 24 Jul 2026, a Causeway Bay flagship (Lee Garden 3) in Hong Kong, branded COMMUNE MAISON.
commune.franchise_note: Chinese dining-bar chain, company-operated (直营). First overseas store Hong Kong (Causeway Bay) Jul 2026; no US presence.

dusu.name: Dusu Bakery
dusu.global: Shanghai bakery chain (读酥世家) — mochi pudding, butter rice cakes, egg tarts, burnt cheesecake and sweet/savory buns. Opened its first US location in 2026 as a shop-in-shop counter inside Duo Duo Snacks (a Chinese snack market) at 5585 Rosemead Blvd, Temple City CA.
dusu.franchise_note: Shanghai bakery chain; first US outlet is a shop-in-shop counter inside Duo Duo Snacks, Temple City CA, tracked on the map via sightings (chain_id 'dusu'). No standalone US locator.

aunteajenny.name: Auntea Jenny
aunteajenny.global: Shanghai freshly-made tea chain (沪上阿姨 'Shanghai Auntie', founded 2013; HKEX 2589, listed 8 May 2025) — grain-forward / 五谷 milk teas, overwhelmingly franchised, ~9,000+ stores almost all in China. Fast overseas push from 2025-26: Malaysia (a dozen+ KL outlets), Australia (Sydney), the UK (London), South Korea (Seoul) and Indonesia (Jakarta). Hong Kong is a listing venue only — no HK retail outlets (its own Global Sites list excludes HK). Collected daily on the US map; its international markets are tracked here.
aunteajenny.franchise_note: Shanghai tea chain (HKEX 2589); overwhelmingly franchised. US estate collected daily (chain_id 'aunteajenny'); overseas markets compiled here. The IPO prospectus (end-2024) showed only 1 overseas store (KL) — the footprint below has grown far beyond that since.

shudaxia.name: Shu Da Xia Hotpot
shudaxia.global: Chengdu wuxia-themed Sichuan hot-pot chain (600+ outlets; owned by the Xiaolongkan group since 2023). Overseas: Malaysia (3 outlets), Australia (3 in Melbourne — Carlton, Carnegie, Box Hill — trading as 'Panda Hot Pot', 蜀大侠火锅) and Canada (Toronto) are open; Singapore (Tampines) and Hong Kong (Causeway Bay) were entered and have since permanently closed. One US restaurant near Boston University since 2022.

shikao.name: Shikao Grilled Fish
shikao.global: Guangzhou-origin Chongqing-style tofu-flower grilled-fish chain (师烤豆花烤鱼; founded ~2019, 170-200+ outlets in China, a top grilled-fish brand, franchise program). Overseas: Singapore (Marine Parade), Canada (Ottawa + Mississauga), and Australia (Sydney Chinatown — a combined 'Shikao × Panda Hotpot 熊猫冲浪火锅' venue). Not yet in the US.

littlesheep.name: Little Sheep
littlesheep.global: Inner Mongolia (Baotou) Mongolian hot-pot chain founded 1999; owned by Yum China since 2012. A global franchise present across East/Southeast Asia and Oceania — Japan, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore, Cambodia, Myanmar, New Zealand, Australia — plus its China home market. After the Yum takeover its founder Zhang Gang (张钢) left and re-created the brand as the DISTINCT Happy Lamb (快乐小羊, 2017), to which Little Sheep's former overseas outlets — including old US ones such as 1737 Route 27, Edison NJ (a Little Sheep in 2014, now a Happy Lamb) — were largely renamed. Little Sheep itself (小肥羊, under Yum China) RE-ENTERED the US in 2026 with a NEW location at the American Dream mall, East Rutherford, NJ (littlesheepusa.com) — not to be confused with Happy Lamb 快乐小羊.

toys52.name: 52TOYS
toys52.global: China-origin collectible-IP / designer-toy company (brand 52TOYS, launched 2015; operator Beijing Lezi Tiancheng Culture Development, 北京乐自天成, founded 2012; CEO Chen Wei 陈威). Full-chain IP-toy maker on an 'own IP + licensed IP' model — own IPs incl. 猛兽匣 Beastbox and 胖哒幼 Panda Roll, licenses incl. Crayon Shin-chan and Tom & Jerry; ~2,800 SKUs, 35 owned + 80 licensed IPs. 3rd-largest IP-toy company by 2024 China GMV. Channel-led: ~2/3 of revenue via dealers/distribution, and own China stores shrank 19→5 (2022–May 2025) even as revenue grew RMB463M→630M (loss-making, loss widening to RMB122M in 2024). Filed a HKEX A1 on 22 May 2025 (sponsors Citi + Huatai); the application lapsed 22 Nov 2025. Overseas via Taiwan (Shin Kong Mitsukoshi counters), a Hong Kong Airport store, and the US (two metro-Atlanta stores).
toys52.franchise_note: China IP-toy maker; US-tracked via two metro-Atlanta stores, with Taiwan counters (Shin Kong Mitsukoshi) abroad. Primarily wholesale/distribution + own stores, not franchise; no US franchise offer or FDD confirmed.

mamaxita.name: Mama Xita BBQ
mamaxita.global: Chinese-Korean-style barbecue chain from the Xita Korean-BBQ district of Shenyang, Liaoning; ~450+ outlets across 31 Asian cities, run by the Chubby Group (also Chubby Cattle). US outlets (Bellevue WA, Temple City CA) tracked via sightings. Entered Hong Kong in 2023 (first store TST East) but FULLY EXITED by 2026 — both HK stores closed, the last foreclosed/auctioned amid rent disputes, after under 3 years. Distinct from 西塔烧烤 / Xi Top BBQ, Flushing.
mamaxita.franchise_note: Chubby Group BBQ chain; US-tracked via Bellevue WA + Temple City CA. Fully exited HK 2026. No US franchise offer or FDD confirmed.

sanjin.name: Sanjin Tangbao
sanjin.global: Soup-dumpling (湯包) and pan-fried-bun QSR chain; brand created in Shenzhen 2014 (operator 深圳三津餐饮管理) by three founders from Huaining, Anhui — 5,300+ franchised stores (May 2023) across Guangdong, Hunan, Fujian, Jiangxi and Guangxi; a '国民早餐' (national breakfast) brand. Entered Hong Kong 20 Sept 2023 (Maxgrand Plaza, San Po Kong) — reportedly the first China soup-dumpling brand in HK; ~3 company-operated HK stores with HK-customised flavours. No known US presence.
sanjin.franchise_note: Shenzhen-based 包点/soup-dumpling franchise (5,300+ China stores). Entered HK 2023 (company-operated). No US presence.

baheli.name: Baheli
aliases: 八合里潮汕鲜牛肉火锅
baheli.global: Chaoshan (潮汕)-style fresh-beef hotpot chain from Shantou, Guangdong; 200+ stores in China. Entered Hong Kong late 2024 — first store trial at New Town Plaza, Sha Tin (Nov 2024; officially opened 5 Dec 2024 per Invest HK), operated by 香港八合里餐飲管理. Planned 2-3 HK stores short-term, but that expansion is as-yet-unrealized; ~1 store (V Walk, Sham Shui Po) confirmed open Oct 2026. No known US presence.
baheli.franchise_note: Shantou Chaoshan beef-hotpot chain (200+ China stores); HK via 香港八合里餐飲管理 (2024). Planned 2-3 HK stores not yet realized. No US presence.

chenpengpeng.name: Teochew Bistro
chenpengpeng.global: Shenzhen-based Chaoshan (潮汕/Teochew) cuisine chain, signature Chaoshan braised goose (卤鹅); grew from a braised-goose restaurant (陈鹏鹏卤鹅饭店, ~2016) into 陈鹏鹏潮汕菜 (~2021) — ~30-34 stores concentrated in Shenzhen/Guangdong. Entered Hong Kong: 1 store at New Town Plaza, Sha Tin (branded 'Teochew Bistro' / 陳鵬鵬潮汕菜). No known US presence.
chenpengpeng.franchise_note: Shenzhen Chaoshan-cuisine chain (~30-34 stores, mostly Guangdong); 1 HK store (New Town Plaza). No US presence.

gulugulu.name: GuluGulu
gulugulu.global: China-origin takoyaki (章魚燒/丸子) and milk-tea snack chain; reportedly founded in Guangzhou in 1997 (a Philippines franchisee cites 600+ China stores — unverified), with China stores (e.g. Shenzhen) and overseas branches (Singapore, Australia, Philippines). Entered Hong Kong — one store at Yau Ma Tei. No known US presence. (Origin/scale to re-verify.)
gulugulu.franchise_note: China-origin takoyaki/snack chain (franchises; 600+ China stores per a franchisee site, unverified); 1 HK store. No US presence.

luobo.name: Luobo Xiangnan
luobo.global: China (Xiangxi / western Hunan)-style fast-food brand — hot-plate fried rice (鐵板炒飯) and Xiangxi pickles. Entered Hong Kong with one store at Dundas Square, Mong Kok (leased Dec 2023, opened Feb 2024) but CLOSED after ~4 months (~June 2024) amid 'poor local fit'. China chain scale UNCONFIRMED — possibly a limited/single venture. No known US presence.
luobo.franchise_note: China Xiangxi/Hunan fast-food brand; one HK store, exited 2024 after ~4 months. China scale unconfirmed. No US presence.

tosummer.name: To Summer
tosummer.global: China-origin niche fragrance / home-scent brand — founded Beijing 2018 (劉惠璞 + 沈黎), 'new Chinese' (新中式) oriental perfumery, L'Oréal-backed; ~10+ China stores incl. Shanghai (湖南路 flagship), Beijing (國子監四合院), Wuxi and Nanjing. Hong Kong first overseas store at Causeway Bay. No known US presence.
tosummer.franchise_note: China-origin fragrance retailer (direct-operated, L'Oréal-backed); HK first overseas store. No US presence.

hla.name: HLA
hla.global: China-origin menswear chain — founded Jiangyin, Jiangsu (周建平, 1988; brand launched ~2002), listed in Shanghai (600398); one of China's largest apparel chains (5,000+ stores). Overseas push includes Singapore (Suntec City, 2018). Signed its first Hong Kong lease in Central. No known US presence.
hla.franchise_note: China menswear giant (consignment/franchise model, 5,000+ China stores); HK store signed but under fit-out. No US presence.

nonggengji.name: Nong Geng Ji
nonggengji.global: China-origin Hunan home-style restaurant chain — founded Shenzhen 2017; direct-operated, with stores across China (Shenzhen, Beijing, Shanghai, Haikou, Zhuhai, Dongguan, Zhongshan) and overseas in Hong Kong and Singapore. A leading Hunan-cuisine brand. Also present in the US (Flushing NY + Rockville MD).
nonggengji.franchise_note: China-origin Hunan chain, direct-operated. US: Flushing NY + Rockville MD. HK: 9 outlets.

laomatou.name: Lao Ma Tou Hot Pot
laomatou.global: China-origin Sichuan hotpot chain (Chengdu; known for a clear 'no-sediment' red-oil broth 無渣紅油湯底, ranked among Chengdu's top hotpot brands). Entered Hong Kong May 2018 with a ~10,000 sq ft Mong Kok flagship; exited HK in 2024 after six years. No known US presence.
laomatou.franchise_note: China (Chengdu) Sichuan hotpot; entered HK 2018, exited 2024. No US presence.

lmm.name: LMM
lmm.global: China-origin hand-smashed lemon-tea (手打檸檬茶, perfume-lemon 香水檸檬) chain with airport-themed stores (founder Guo Zhenye 郭震業); a 'river-crossing dragon' (過江龍) that entered Hong Kong in 2023. Exited HK in 2024. No known US presence. Distinct from Ningji 柠季, NingQi 柠気 and LINLEE 鄰里.
lmm.franchise_note: China hand-smashed lemon-tea brand; entered HK 2023, exited 2024. No US presence.

chajiu.name: Jo's Cha
chajiu.global: China-origin tea chain (Guangzhou) specializing in seasonal fruit- and vegetable-based teas. Entered Hong Kong and peaked at about 7 stores; has since downsized to ~5 amid the China F&B HK shakeout. No known US presence.
chajiu.franchise_note: China (Guangzhou) seasonal fruit/veg tea chain; HK downsized ~7->5. No US presence.

fufuland.name: fufuland
fufuland.global: China-origin fresh-milk soufflé (生乳舒芙蕾) dessert chain; a 'river-crossing dragon' that entered Hong Kong in 2024 with its sister brand 檸季 (Ningji) and peaked at ~11 HK stores before collapsing and fully exiting HK by July 2026. No known US presence. Origin company not firmly established.
fufuland.franchise_note: China soufflé/dessert brand; entered HK 2024 with sister brand Ningji, peaked ~11 stores, fully exited by Jul 2026. No US presence. Origin company unconfirmed.

laoxianghao.name: Lao Xiang Hao
laoxianghao.global: China-origin Hunan (湘) home-style stir-fry restaurant; a 'river-crossing dragon' (過江龍) that entered Hong Kong with a Mong Kok store but withdrew within months. China chain scale unconfirmed. No known US presence.
laoxianghao.franchise_note: China Hunan stir-fry brand; one HK store, exited 2025 after ~3 months. China scale unconfirmed. No US presence.

xishu.name: CHEZ CHOUX
xishu.global: China-origin cream-puff (泡芙) chain — founded in Shanghai (brand launched ~2010-2011; operated by Shanghai Moti Gongfang 上海摩提工房, est. 2003). Trades internationally as CHEZ CHOUX ('home of puffs'); ~400-700+ stores in China, with the parent group running 1,000+ stores across 150+ cities incl. Hong Kong. Present in HK with 10+ branches plus a new sub-line 'Puffin'. No known US presence.
xishu.franchise_note: China (Shanghai) cream-puff chain (franchises in China); HK 10+ stores as CHEZ CHOUX + Puffin sub-line. No US presence.

luofen.name: Luo Fen Shi Jia
luofen.global: China-origin Jiangxi rice-noodle (江西米粉) brand from Nanchang; a 'river-crossing dragon' that entered Hong Kong with one Cheung Sha Wan store but withdrew after about a year. China chain scale unconfirmed. No known US presence. (HK operator billed as 花姐姐餐飲香港集團.)
luofen.franchise_note: China (Nanchang, Jiangxi) rice-noodle brand; one HK store, exited 2024. China scale unconfirmed. No US presence.

meowbbq.name: Meow BBQ
meowbbq.global: China-origin cat-themed barbecue (烤肉/燒肉) chain — founded 2012 by Fang Daqiang ('Uncle Meow'); combines Japanese-style meat selection, Korean-style marinade and Chinese cooking. 30+ stores across ~10 China cities (Beijing, Guangzhou, Shanghai, Chongqing); repeatedly ranked a Top-10 China BBQ brand. Overseas in Singapore (Bugis+ 2022, VivoCity 2024). Entered then exited Hong Kong. No known US presence.
meowbbq.franchise_note: China-origin BBQ chain (30+ China stores); overseas SG; entered+exited HK. No US presence.

yaoyao.name: YAOYAO
yaoyao.global: China-origin Sichuan pickled-fish (酸菜魚) chain — founded Shenzhen Aug 2016 (founder Yao Minxi 姚旻汐, ex-Huawei); Tiffany-blue bear-fish branding, ~50-70 China stores, repeatedly a Top-10 China pickled-fish brand. Overseas: Singapore (VivoCity 2023) and the US — 3 outlets (Chicago IL, Michelin Bib Gourmand 2024-25; plus San Leandro and San Bruno CA). Entered then fully exited Hong Kong (4 stores, all closed).
yaoyao.franchise_note: China (Shenzhen) pickled-fish chain (franchises since 2019); US 3 stores (Chicago Michelin Bib + 2 CA); HK fully exited.

entries.note: The second retreat-and-return in this register, after CHAGEE in Singapore.
